original_question: On which chromosome is the gene associated with autosomal recessive isolated ectopia lentis located?

final_qi.question: On which chromosome is the gene associated with autosomal recessive isolated ectopia lentis located?
final_qi.long_answer: Autosomal recessive isolated ectopia lentis is caused by loss-of-function mutations in the ADAMTSL4 gene. ADAMTSL4 is mapped to the 1q21 region of chromosome 1, so the pathogenic gene responsible for this condition is located on chromosome 1.

final_answer.long_answer: Autosomal recessive isolated ectopia lentis is most commonly caused by biallelic mutations in the ADAMTSL4 gene.
